This integration connects Gladys to a **Huawei 4G/5G router** or **HiLink USB
stick** (B310, B315, B525, B535, B618, B818, E5186, E5576, E3372h, 5G CPE…).
It shows the signal, the data rates and the data used this month, sends SMS
from your scenes and starts a scene when an SMS arrives or the connection
drops.

## Before you start

- **Gladys 5.3 or later** is required.
- Gladys must reach the router on your local network: open its web page
  (usually `http://192.168.8.1`) from the computer that runs Gladys to check.
- Have the **password of the router web page** at hand. Everything stays on
  your network: the integration never uses the internet nor a Huawei account.

## Configuration

| Field                            | What to put                                                                    |
| -------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Router address                   | The address of its web page, `http://192.168.8.1` by default                   |
| Username                         | `admin` on almost every model                                                  |
| Password                         | The password of the web page; empty for a HiLink stick without login           |
| Refresh interval (s)             | How often the router is read (15 to 3600 s, 60 by default)                     |
| Watch incoming SMS               | Starts the "An SMS is received" trigger for each new message                   |
| Mark handled SMS as read         | Marks the message read on the router once the trigger fired                    |
| Control buttons on the dashboard | Shows "Send an SMS", "Mobile data" and "Reboot" on the widget (off by default) |

Then click **Test the connection**: the answer gives the model, the operator,
the network type and the signal. **Send a test SMS** checks the SIM card can
send messages.

## What you get in Gladys

Once the router is read, it appears in the **Discovery** tab. Add it: it
brings these features.

| Feature                    | Unit     | Notes                                     |
| -------------------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------- |
| Signal (bars)              | 0 to 5   | As the router shows it                    |
| RSRP, RSRQ, SINR           | dBm, dB  | Radio quality, useful to place the router |
| Internet connected         | 0 / 1    | 1 when the mobile connection is up        |
| Download / upload rate     | Mbit/s   | Current rates                             |
| Data downloaded / uploaded | GB       | This month, as counted by the router      |
| Connected for              | minutes  | Length of the current connection          |
| Mobile data                | on / off | The only feature you can control          |
| Unread SMS                 | number   |                                           |
| Network type, operator     | text     | e.g. `LTE+`, `Orange F`                   |
| WAN IP address             | text     | The address given by the operator         |

A value your model does not give is simply not shown.

## Scenes

### Triggers

- **An SMS is received**: a new message arrived in the router inbox. You can
  keep only one sender (the number exactly as the router shows it, e.g.
  `+33612345678`). The scene gets the **sender**, the **message** and the
  **date**.
- **The internet connection changes**: the router connects, loses the mobile
  network, or stops answering ("Router unreachable"). Pick the states you
  want. The scene gets the new and previous state, the network type and the
  operator.

### Actions

- **Send an SMS**: to up to 5 numbers separated by commas. The message can use
  scene variables (e.g. the temperature of a sensor).
- **Reboot the router**: internet is cut for one to three minutes. The
  "Router unreachable" the reboot causes does not start a scene.

## Dashboard widget

The **Huawei LTE router** widget shows the signal, the rates, the data used
this month, the connection, the network type, the operator and the unread
SMS. The WAN IP address is hidden unless you turn on **Show the WAN IP
address** in the widget settings.

The buttons that act on the router (**Send an SMS**, **Mobile data**,
**Reboot**) only appear when **Control buttons on the dashboard** is on in the
configuration: anyone who sees the dashboard can use them.

## SMS

- At the very first start, the messages already waiting in the inbox do not
  start any scene: only the ones received afterwards do.
- With **Mark handled SMS as read** off, the integration remembers the
  messages it already handled (in its own storage), so a restart does not
  start the same scene twice.
- New messages are seen at each refresh (60 s by default).
- Huawei routers store a limited number of messages: empty the inbox from time
  to time from the router web page.

## Troubleshooting

| Message                                     | What to do                                                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| The router does not answer                  | Check the address, and that Gladys runs on the same network as the router                    |
| The router refused the username or password | Retype the password of the web page. The integration waits 10 minutes before trying it again |
| The router locked its login                 | Too many wrong attempts: wait a few minutes, then test again                                 |
| The router asks for a login                 | Fill in the password                                                                         |

The router allows only a few sessions at once: if its web page says too many
users are logged in, log out of the web page or wait a few minutes.

## Privacy and security

- The password is stored by Gladys as a secret and only sent to the router.
- The integration only talks to the router address you gave, on your local
  network.
- The content of SMS is only given to your scenes, never written to the logs.

## Configuration settings

These are the settings Huawei LTE asks for in its configuration screen in Gladys.

| Setting | Type | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Getting started | `section` | No | The integration talks to your Huawei router on your local network, like its web page does: give it the router address and the password of its web page (the one you use on http:\/\/192.168.8.1). Nothing goes through the internet or a Huawei account. |
| Router address | `string` | Yes | Address of the router web page, usually http:\/\/192.168.8.1. |
| Username | `string` | No | User of the router web page, almost always admin. |
| Password | `secret` | No | Password of the router web page. Leave empty for a HiLink USB stick without login. |
| Refresh interval (s) | `number` | No | How often the router is read, in seconds (15 to 3600). New SMS are seen at the same pace. |
| Watch incoming SMS | `boolean` | No | Fire the "SMS received" scene trigger for each new message. |
| Mark handled SMS as read | `boolean` | No | Once the trigger fired, the message is marked read on the router. |
| Control buttons on the dashboard | `boolean` | No | Show "Send an SMS", "Mobile data" and "Reboot" on the widget. Anyone who sees the dashboard can use them. |

## How to install Huawei LTE in Gladys

1. In Gladys, open **Integrations**: Huawei LTE appears in the catalog, next to the native integrations, with a community badge.
2. Click **Install**. Gladys pulls the Docker image (`ghcr.io/prohand/gladys-huawailte:1.0.1`), starts it in a sandbox isolated from the core, and generates the integration's interface (devices, discovery and configuration).
3. Open the **Configuration** screen of the integration, fill in the settings, and save.
4. You can also install it directly from its repository URL: [https://github.com/prohand/gladys-huawailte](https://github.com/prohand/gladys-huawailte).

Huawei LTE requires Gladys `>=5.3.0`. The catalog inside Gladys refreshes every hour, so a new version becomes available at most one hour after its release.

Not running Gladys yet? It is free and open source: [follow the installation guide](/docs/) to get started.

## About external integrations

Huawei LTE is an **external integration**: a community integration packaged as a Docker container and published on GitHub, that Gladys installs in one click and runs in a sandbox isolated from its core. It is published and maintained by [prohand](https://github.com/prohand), not by the Gladys core team.
